messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday we're seeing p99 latency creeping up on cross-zone traffic. Not huge but noticeable: p50 stable, p95 up ~10%, p99 up ~30%.

kai: ugh. do you have numbers?

maria: short summary from our profiler: before change p50=85ms p95=180ms p99=420ms. after change p50=88ms p95=200ms p99=540ms. traces show extra KV cache misses and more cross-zone RPCs when spillover kicks in.

sam: can you paste the trace with the KV miss?

maria: sure — snippet from trace where request spilled to eu-west and lost hot KV prefix: 
```
REQ start -> local queue wait 8ms -> batch formed(3) -> kernel select remote-quantized -> remote fetch KV miss -> remote RPC 42ms -> rehydrate KV -> token gen -> finish
```

nina: so kernel change is indirectly increasing cross-zone fetches? interesting.

kai: my guess — kernel selection now prefers a quantized variant in other zone for certain seq length combos, so the smart router sends to that zone when local pool is saturated. affinity_weight got lowered in 176 deploy.

maria: yes. affinity_weight went 0.85 -> 0.6 in that deploy. also token_budget_ms for batch formation lowered to 10ms -> smaller batches -> more frequent KV lookups.

sam: tradeoff: smaller token_budget reduces latency for short reqs but increases tail for some workloads due to cache churn and cross-zone RPCs.

eng-runtime-bot: deploy 176.9 rolled at 2025-11-03T19:02Z by kai :rocket:

maria: did a quick experiment on a canary cluster (eu-west primary, us-east spill). changed two things: affinity_weight back to 0.8, token_budget_ms 14, and added soft-spill hysteresis (5s) so we avoid flipping hot prefixes between zones. results (30m run, mixed traffic): p50 86ms p95 185ms p99 325ms. KV miss rate down ~42%.

kai: that's promising. what's the cost delta?

maria: small — GPU utilization in eu-west rose ~4% (we kept capacity static). overall cross-zone RPCs down 60% so egress costs dropped. local tail reduced.

nina: can you share the config snippet you used?

maria: pasted below: 
```
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_ms: 14
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
queue_policy:
  affinity_weight: 0.8
  spill_threshold: 0.9
  soft_spill_hysteresis_s: 5
  allow_cross_zone_spill: true
kv_cache:
  prefix_pin_ttl_s: 300
  eviction_policy: lru
```

sam: nice. two concerns: (1) hysteresis might delay legitimate balancing during sustained imbalances, (2) increasing affinity could leave some zones underutilized during traffic spikes. we should run a stress test.

kai: agree. propose: run 4h A/B on canary with traffic replay: baseline (current prod) vs candidate (maria's config). capture p50/p95/p99, KV hit rate, cross-zone RPC count, GPU util per zone, and cost estimate.

maria: done quickly locally — but will run full 4h job tomorrow. i also instrumented a per-prefix hot-score so we can prefer pinning top-5% hot prefixes locally. that reduced thrash in canary.

nina: good. also we should look at kernel selector heuristics: maybe prefer same-zone kernels when delta perf < 6% to avoid cost of KV/egress. that rule would cut only small perf gains but save tails.

sam: can we express that as a tie-break in kernel selector? pseudo: 
```
if (latency_gain < 6% && kernel_zone != request_zone) prefer same_zone_kernel
```

kai: yep. add metric for "secondary-kernel-cost": includes kv-miss penalty + egress. we can learn threshold automatically later.

maria: quick profiling note: the KV cache serialization path got slightly slower due to a small memcopy introduced in the kernel-change PR. profiling shows +0.8ms median on local rehydrate. i'll send a micro-PR to remove that copy. should shave a bit off p95.

sam: good catch. small regressions compound.

eng-runtime-bot: perf alert (p99) — routed to eng-runtime on 2025-11-04T02:20Z

kai: action list: 
- maria -> run 4h A/B (canary) with candidate config, collect metrics (owner: maria)
- kai -> add kernel-selector same-zone tie-break and metric for secondary-kernel-cost (owner: kai)
- nina -> run cost model for config delta and provide recommendation (owner: nina)
- sam -> review KV serialization micro-PR and bench (owner: sam)

maria: i'll post results here when done, ETA 24h. tagging @oncall to watch the canary windows. :eyes:

nina: sgtm. if canary looks good we can do staged rollout w/ rollout policy: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> all, with auto-rollback on p99 regression >10%.

sam: also suggest adding a small token_budget hysteresis: don't change token_budget for a prefix more than once every 30s to avoid oscillation.

kai: ok adding to ticket. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — will report back.
